title: POC scoping: burst & fallback sizing — SableForge pilot
summary: Discovery + POC sizing focused on reserved GPU baseline, burst credits, and fallback to quantized small-models. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot with a synthetic throughput benchmark and a real-traffic shadow run. Success criteria centered on cost per 1k tokens, p95/p99 latency, and failover correctness for degraded models.
topics: Benchmark plan: synthetic and shadow runs
transcript:
Header: 2026-11-17 11:00 PT | Duration 52 min | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Carlos (SE), Liam (SableForge Head ML), Maya (Platform), Rohan (CTO), Greta (Sec)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll kick off - quick intros, then jump into the sizing and the POC plan.
[00:15] Liam: thanks, jordan, quick hello everyone - we want to validate cost and reliability for our generative summarization flows. Typical batch is 600 concurrent users during peak, with some spikes up to 1.2k.
[00:34] Priya: got it. when you say 600 concurrent, is that concurrent requests or concurrent tokens-in-flight?
[00:40] Liam: concurrent requests, average prompt length ~350 tokens, responses ~750 tokens - so tokens-in-flight on average is roughly 650k tokens per minute at peak. Might be noisy.
[01:05] Maya: and we run in eu-west for compliance reasons, so regional capacity matters. Also we need private deployment eventually, VPC, and KMS for keys.
[01:18] Priya: perfect. for the POC we typically recommend a reserved baseline sized to cover steady state (say 70-80% of your 95th) and then a burst pool for spikes. Two mechanisms: dedicated GPU reservation plus an elastic burst bucket, or rely on a warm standby pool.
[01:36] Rohan: what's the tradeoff here? cost vs latency?
[01:39] Carlos: yeah, cost is mainly reserved GPU uptime. burst handles spikes but you pay for burst in unit-hours or credits. If you rely on cold-start VMs that can add latency; warm pool keeps VMs ready but costs more.
[01:55] Greta: security questions - is the burst path still within our VPC for Private deployment? we can't route through a public multi-tenant plane.
[02:03] Jordan: for Private/Pilot we run the control plane in Redwood but traffic and inference run in your VPC — burst still stays in your environment if we deploy Private; for hosted pilot we can do VPC peering or private link. we'll send the architecture diagram.
[02:22] Liam: ok, success criteria — we want p95 under 450ms and p99 under 900ms for single-turn generative calls, cost under $0.60 per 1k output tokens, and no failed responses on fallback.
[02:36] Priya: that's clear. for fallback policies we propose a tiered degrade: full model -> quantized variant -> smaller fallback model. KV/prefix cache reused across variants to keep context warm. In practice we do model-compatibility checks and automatic re-routing.
[02:55] Maya: how does cache work when falling back to smaller models? is the KV compatible?
[03:00] Priya: not directly — we do prefix/KV translation when possible; otherwise we warm with the last N tokens. there's sometimes a small mismatch, you'll see slight quality variance but semantics preserved.
[03:18] Rohan: will that cause hallucinations?
[03:21] Priya: shouldn't, but quality thresholds and scoring will trigger a fallback to the previous variant if we detect regressions. we also run evaluation prompts concurrently during pilot to monitor quality drift.
[03:40] Liam: benchmarks - what do you need from us to size the baseline?
[03:44] Carlos: sample traffic trace (15-30 days) or synthetic QPS + token distribution. For initial POC if traces are sensitive just give aggregated histograms: requests/sec distribution, token lengths, percentiles.
[04:00] Liam: we can provide a week of anonymized logs.
[04:04] Jordan: great. here's our proposed benchmark plan: 1) synthetic ramp test to determine throughput at different batch sizes and quantization levels, 2) shadow run for 72 hours against real traffic at 10-20% sampling, 3) failover exercise where we intentionally drain baseline to validate fallback policies.
[04:24] Maya: during shadow run we must ensure logs and PII never leave our VPC; do you support token redaction and audit logs?
[04:32] Jordan: yes, token redaction options, and we can restrict logs to your KMS-encrypted storage. we have SOC2 docs - we'll share.
[04:40] Rohan: timeline?
[04:42] Priya: proposed: week 0 - onboarding and infra setup (VPC peering, service account, KMS), week 1 - synthetic benchmarks, week 2 - shadow run and failover tests, week 3 - analysis and recommendation. so ~3 weeks. you said earlier you wanted a two-week pilot?
[05:00] Liam: shorter preferred, 2 weeks is fine if we compress onboarding.
[05:05] Jordan: we can compress to 2 weeks if SableForge can provide anonymized logs and quick network approvals. onboarding checklist we'll send today.
[05:14] Greta: on SSO and audit, we need SAML and RBAC to map roles. also retention and audit retention policies for debug traces.
[05:24] Carlos: supported — RBAC via SAML + SCIM sync, audit retention configurable. we'll include the admin flow in the docs.
[05:32] Maya: curious about fallback correctness — can we run a canary where 5% of traffic is forced to fallback path to compare outputs?
[05:39] Priya: yes, canary and A/B tests are supported. we also provide evaluation hooks so you can compute rouge/semantic similarity metrics off the outputs.
[05:49] Liam: about numbers — we'd like a conservative reserved baseline that covers p90 of steady traffic and burst for up to 2x for short periods. what's your recommendation in GPUs?
[05:58] Priya: from your numbers (600 steady, 1.2k spikes, token lengths) initial recommendation: 4x A100-40GB (reserved) covering steady throughput with batch config, plus 1-2x on-demand GPUs as warm pool for spikes. If you plan to quantize heavily we can drop to 2 reserved + bigger burst.
[06:19] Rohan: and fallback models? sizes?
[06:21] Priya: main model is a 70B style with float16 / qat 4-bit option; quantized variant is 8-bit with slight perf boost; fallback is a 7B quantized model for high availability. routing policy: prefer baseline, if queueing > threshold route to quantized variant, if latency breach route to 7B fallback, with confidence scoring.
[06:44] Maya: what about cold-starts for burst GPUs - how long to warm?
[06:47] Carlos: cold start of a new GPU node is ~45-120s depending on image and model pulling; warm pool keeps the kube pod hot ~10-20s to attach. So warm pool is recommended for sub-2min spikes.
[06:58] Liam: cost estimation?
[07:00] Jordan: we'll send a cost modeling spreadsheet but rough: reserved 4x A100 monthly amortized + 1-2x burst credit. We'll give per-1k token estimate for your workload after synthetic run.
[07:12] Greta: compliance — any attestation for on-prem private deployment?
[07:16] Jordan: we support private on-prem install for enterprise engagements with extra SLA and audit support; that conversation will be via our Solutions Architecture lead.
[07:26] Maya: success criteria recap?
[07:28] Liam: p95 <450ms, p99 <900ms, cost < $0.60 per 1k tokens, <0.1% failed requests during failover, and quality parity >= 95% similarity vs baseline on evaluation prompts.
[07:44] Priya: captured. we'll instrument eval prompts and produce dashboards for those metrics.
[07:51] Jordan: next steps: we'll send onboarding checklist, benchmark plan, and cost model. can we aim for kickoff next Monday 2026-11-23?
[08:01] Rohan: that works, pending sign-off.
[08:03] Liam: yes, aim for that.
[08:05] Jordan: ok i'll follow up with action items. thanks everyone.
[08:10] Speaker 1: end recording.
